title: His father's homemade drum set and what became of it
summary: Describes his father's wooden trap pedal, Chinese cymbals, blocks and cowbells; his mother got rid of the set and he later bought his own.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: dance drum set with bass drum and snare and everything? That's right. Set up like they do now in the jazz band? Well, it was a little different. I've heard he made his own foot pedal. Oh yes, in the old days they had one. Yeah.

He didn't have an overhead foot pedal. He had one made in a trap form because it's different in foot pedals. And an overhead foot pedal and a trap foot pedal was made out of wood. But these days they are made out of iron, but they're traps. Yeah. But in those days they were considered as overhead traps. Yeah.
But he made one out of wood. Do you remember, was there a cymbal in the drum set?

Yeah, they had craft cymbals. The Chinese? The craft cymbals, yeah that's right. A Chinese cymbal was called a craft cymbal. He had blocks. Any cowbells like your ears? Yeah, he had cowbells. My bells is not exactly cowbells, they're orchestra bells and his was cowbells at that time. Yeah.
Um, did you just keep your same drum set then that your father had and...
No, my mother got rid of the set that my father had. It was a new leader set. And she got rid of that. And when I come up to play, I got my own set.
